_comment: General tips for the Seine page's AI cruise finder. Facts only from seine-river-cruises-paris (Before You Book, cards, reviews). No guest-review themes collected yet, so 'cruises' is empty.
general: Most boats leave from the Eiffel Tower piers (Port de la Bourdonnais for Bateaux Parisiens, Port de Suffren for Vedettes de Paris). Bateaux Mouches is at Pont de l'Alma, about 15 minutes on foot from the tower.
After dark the Eiffel Tower sparkles for 5 minutes at the start of every hour. Time a night sailing to pass it then.
Every large boat has a heated, enclosed cabin, so rain only costs you the open deck. The private boat (#7) is the exception.
Bateaux Parisiens and Bateaux Mouches tickets work on any sailing that day; no time slot to book. In summer, arrive 15 to 20 minutes early.
The classic 1-hour sightseeing cruises follow the same loop from the Eiffel Tower past the Louvre to Notre-Dame and back; what differs is the boat, the seats, the commentary and the pier.
Bateaux Parisiens (#1) top-deck benches face sideways; Bateaux Mouches (#2) has front-facing seats on a huge open deck.
For a live guide: Vedettes de Paris guided electric boat (#6, English), the Canal Saint-Martin cruise (#5, English and French) and the amphibious bus (#10, English and French).
Cheapest: Bateaux Mouches (#2) at €17 and Bateaux Parisiens (#1) at €18 per adult. Kids under 4 ride free on both.
Bateaux Parisiens: restrooms are only on the boats, not on the docks, and there is a bag check at boarding; large luggage is not accepted.
